steps: Pressure cook the sprouted matki with a pinch of the turmeric and water to cover on medium heat for 1 whistle. Keep the water.
Heat the oil on medium heat and add the mustard and cumin seeds. When they pop, add the curry leaves and hing.
Add most of the onion and fry for 3 to 4 minutes until light brown, then add the crushed ginger and garlic for 2 minutes.
Add the tomato and salt and cook, stirring, until soft and mushy.
Stir in the rest of the turmeric, the chilli powder, coriander powder and garam masala and cook for about 2 minutes, until oil shows.
Add the matki with its water and more water to make about 250 ml a person. Boil, then simmer on medium for 5 to 10 minutes.
Slit the pav, spread it with the butter and toast it on a pan on medium heat until lightly golden.
Ladle the misal into bowls, top with sev, the rest of the onion, coriander and a squeeze of lemon, and serve with the pav.
note: After the 8-hour soak the matki needs about a day more wrapped in a damp cloth to sprout, so start two days ahead. Garam masala stands in for goda or misal masala, which the pack does not have, and sev stands in for farsan.
